To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) fts gene expression is regulated by DnaA protein and that the effect of Dna protein levels on fts transcription can be detected in vivo, and (ii) fts gene transcription is also regulated by the rate of initiation of replication.
fts gene transcription responds both to reduced DnaA levels, as in a dnaA(ts) strain, and to elevated DnaA levels in dnaA overproducing strains.
fts transcription responds to both the level and the activity of DnaA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the cell division genes fta, ftsB, ftsQ and F.
the control of the expression of genes involved in the cell division cycle in Escherichia coil, and in particular with the regulation of the ftsQ gene.
the control of cell division in Escherichia col.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DnaA controls fts gene expression, but the mechanism is complex and may differ from that of dnaA gene regulation.
DnaA regulates transcription of both fts and dnaA genes but, at least in some cases, the effect of Dna protein on fts gene expression is mediated indirectly by its effect on initiation at oriC.
fts gene transcription responds to both changes in Dna protein level and the rate of replication initiation at oriC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DnaA controls fts expression in vivo but the effect of DnaB and DnaC on this process is complex.

DnaA regulates fts and dnaA gene expression by binding to a defined sequence at the promoter region of each gene, and that this binding can be modulated by DnaA protein concentration and the rate of origin initiation.
fts and dnaA transcription respond differently to changes in Dina protein levels and to the rate of oriC initiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of initiation of replication, and not just the intracellular level of DnaA per se, can have a major impact on fts gene transcription.
the fts genes respond to the rate of DNA replication and to DnaA levels, and that the dnaA gene responds only to changes in DmaA levels.
ftsQ transcription responds to both the level of DnaA in the cell and the rate of replication.
